narrative.overview: Tharros Canada is an evidence-led commercial research house. Warm ivory carries graphite ink, dark bands mark major commercial/task moments, and light document headers keep archive, methodology, expertise and policy pages editorial. The visual material comes from real research artifacts and official-source data rather than stock photography or generic dashboard cards.\n\nThe homepage starts from client decisions, then expertise, live Statistics Canada evidence, services and the research archive. Public research remains visibly empty until verified work exists. Market Data fails closed when official sources are unavailable.
keyCharacteristics: Ivory ground, graphite ink, dark bands used selectively rather than on every route.
Services · Expertise · Research · Market Data · About primary navigation.
Four hero modes: home, standard, task and light document.
Research archive built for search/filter growth but honest while empty.
Official Statistics Canada data with visible provenance and limitations; no synthetic fallback.
Ruled registers and 12-column layouts instead of cards.
Red for action, steel for data, green for positive state/change.
Source Serif 4 editorial voice and Schibsted Grotesk interface voice.

rules.name: The Red Means Act Rule
rules.body: Red marks something the visitor can do. It never tints a surface, never colours a datum, and never decorates a heading.

rules.name: The Data Channel Rule
rules.body: Steel carries series and magnitudes, and green carries positive change and confirmation. Neither is used for action or ornament.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Dark tones appear only as full-bleed chapter bands and the footer, never as boxes on the ivory ground. Inside a band, every colour switches to its on-dark partner, including focus.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading as a label. Uppercase appears only as a field label for data, placed directly above the value it names.

rules.name: The Meaningful Numeral Rule
rules.body: Numbering (01–05, 1–3, the success-step counter) is used only where the sequence carries meaning: the five-question index, process and request steps, and HS headings. Numerals are always tabular and slate.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure a reader compares (chart labels, shares, prices, change readouts, progress) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The One Rule Per Boundary Rule
rules.body: Each boundary gets exactly one rule. A strong 1px ink (or 2px on entry heads and sidebars) opens a list or entry, and hairline rules divide its rows. Never double a rule with padding boxes or borders on both sides.

rules.name: The Printed Plate Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift or float. Hover changes colour, underline or arrow position, never elevation.

dos: **Do** use official source metadata and real research artifacts as visual content.
**Do** keep publisher, period, retrieval/release context and limitations near quantitative claims.
**Do** keep the research archive empty until verified work exists.
**Do** use light document headers for editorial and policy pages.
**Do** retain accessible table/text equivalents for charts.
**Do** fail closed when an official data source is unavailable.
donts: **Don't** fabricate reports, clients, experts, partnerships, awards, images or findings.
**Don't** substitute synthetic values when Statistics Canada or another official source fails.
**Don't** use government logos or marks to imply affiliation.
**Don't** add decorative dashboard cards, stock photography or ornamental charts.
**Don't** use a large dark hero on every page.
**Don't** let indicative price ranges become the main brand proposition.
